intro: Real testing runs on your machine: the model under test is a local open-weight model (Ollama) or Claude on your own subscription, and the grader is your coding agent or a local model. No API key, nothing metered.

sections.title: Claude Code plugin
sections.body: Claude Code attacks and tests your agent's prompt on a real model, grades the answers itself, and hands you the report card and the fix. Fusion mixes in questions with known answers, so every card shows how accurate the grading was in that run.

steps.label: Install
steps.code:
claude plugin marketplace add /path/to/fusion
claude plugin install fusion@fusion-first
ollama pull llama3.2:1b

sections.title: Command line
sections.body: The same engine without an agent. Pick a local grader, or grade the questions yourself with tasks and submit.

steps.label: Test a prompt end to end
steps.code:
fusion run start --prompt agent.txt --target ollama:llama3.2:1b --grader ollama-prob:qwen2.5:7b
fusion run finalize --min-grade B

steps.label: Grade your agent's existing logs (no attacks)
steps.code: fusion run logs --file logs.jsonl --check everything --grader ollama-prob:qwen2.5:7b

steps.label: Already use promptfoo? Get intervals and a paired test on its results

sections.title: This web app, on your machine
sections.body: The same scan wizard, driving your local models. It only listens on 127.0.0.1, and every request that runs anything must carry a random token that only the page it opened holds, so no website you visit can use your models.

sections.title: Any MCP client
sections.body: Cursor, Windsurf or your own agent: the fusion-mcp server exposes the same run tools (start_run, get_grading_tasks, submit_grades, finalize_run) plus one-shot scan, harden and runtime-check tools.

sections.title: CI, offline
sections.body: Every run is recorded under .fusion/runs. Commit a run and CI re-derives its result offline, with no model or key. It checks the run tested the prompt you ship, and fails the build below your bar. A withheld grade always fails.

steps.label: In your pipeline
steps.code:
fusion run verify $RUN_ID --prompt agent.txt
fusion run finalize $RUN_ID --min-grade B

sections.title: Runtime guard
sections.body: Prompt fixes reduce issues; the runtime guard catches what still slips through. Wrap your model client in code, or add the opt-in fusion-guard plugin so Claude Code asks before exfiltration, destructive commands or settings tampering. It never auto-allows.

steps.label: In your agent's code
steps.code:
from fusion.guardrail.guard import Guardrail
from fusion.guardrail.policy import GuardConfig
from fusion.guardrail.client import GuardedModelClient

guard = Guardrail(GuardConfig(allowlisted_domains=["your-co.com"], system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT))
client = GuardedModelClient(your_model_client, guard)
